name: Cortistatin-14

lead: Cortistatin-14 is a short neuropeptide closely related to somatostatin, first noted for its activity in the cortex. Occasional recovery and GH-axis speculation comes from the fact that it also binds ghrelin-type receptors.

It shares 11 of 14 amino acids with somatostatin-14, binds all five somatostatin receptors, has been reported to bind GHS receptors in human pituitary tissue, and activates the itch receptor MRGPRX2. The literature is basic neuroscience, receptor pharmacology and a few small human endocrine studies. No trial has tested it for appearance, muscle or recovery.

paras: It is a research peptide with no approved product, so there is no established routine. It appears in discussion mainly as a curiosity in the GH and recovery space.
Human safety data are essentially limited to small endocrine studies. It has no approved product or regulatory status as a medicine, and its itch-receptor activity is one documented effect.

angle.text: Cortistatin-14 is a brain neuropeptide related to somatostatin that also binds ghrelin-type receptors, which draws occasional speculation about recovery and the GH axis. Published work is basic science and receptor pharmacology.

lead: Cortistatin-14 is a naturally occurring neuropeptide related to somatostatin. It was named for its predominantly cortical expression and its ability to depress cortical activity, and it shares 11 of its 14 amino acids with somatostatin-14 even though the two peptides are encoded by separate genes [1][2].

Unlike somatostatin, cortistatin has been reported to bind growth hormone secretagogue (GHS) receptors in human pituitary tissue, and it binds all five cloned somatostatin receptors [1][3]. More recently, structural work identified it as an endogenous agonist of the itch-related receptor MRGPRX2 [4]. It is a research peptide and has no approved medical use.

No published human study has tested cortistatin-14 for any appearance-related purpose. The literature consists of basic neuroscience, receptor pharmacology and a small number of human endocrine studies.

paras: Cortistatin was cloned from human, mouse and rat sources and is known to bind all five cloned somatostatin receptors, sharing many pharmacological properties with somatostatin while also having distinct physiological functions [1][2].

A study of human pituitary membranes reported that cortistatin, but not somatostatin, bound to GHS receptors, the same receptor family targeted by ghrelin [3]. Ghrelin binding sites have also been characterised in human hypothalamus and pituitary tissue [5].

Cryo-electron microscopy structures of MRGPRX2, a mast-cell and itch receptor, bound to cortistatin-14 were published in 2021, identifying the peptide as an endogenous ligand of that receptor [4][6][7].

No studies of cortistatin-14 for appearance, muscle, recovery or growth outcomes were found. A human endocrine study examined the peptide's activities and its interaction with GHRH and ghrelin [8]. Other work is laboratory-based, including receptor expression in human macrophages for somatostatin receptor subtypes [9] and somatostatin knockout mouse studies [10].
